transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?
I guess… I came in because I’ve been feeling really low for a long time. Most mornings I wake up and it’s already there, like this heavy gray feeling, and it kind of follows me through the day.
How long have you been feeling this way? When did you first notice these feelings starting?
It’s been… a little over two years. About two years and a couple months, I think. It started around when the staffing changed at the clinic and my schedule got all over the place.
Have you had any periods of time during these two years where your mood improved, even briefly?
Not really… maybe little moments here and there, but it doesn’t really lift. I usually wake up already feeling low, and it just kind of stays with me through the day.
Have you noticed any changes in your sleep — like trouble falling asleep, waking up during the night, or sleeping much more than usual?
I don’t know… I haven’t really paid close attention to it. My sleep’s not something I can explain well.
Have you lost interest in things you used to enjoy, like hobbies, activities, or spending time with people?
I’m not really sure. I mean… I don’t do much outside of work anyway, so it’s hard to tell. Some stuff just feels harder to get into, I guess.
Have you noticed that things you used to enjoy, like hobbies or time with friends, feel less interesting or less pleasurable lately?
I’m not sure. I don’t really do much of that stuff lately, so it’s hard to tell if it’s less enjoyable or if I’m just… not doing it.
When you do have free time or engage in activities, do you find that they don’t bring you the same sense of enjoyment or pleasure as they used to?
I don’t really know. I don’t do enough to compare it, I guess. If I’m just sitting around or watching something, it’s… fine, maybe. Not sure I’d call it enjoyment.

Can you think back to things you used to enjoy before this started — like hobbies, activities, or time with friends — and whether those things felt as good or pleasurable as they used to when you did them?
I don’t really know. I’m having a hard time thinking of anything specific. I guess I just don’t pay that much attention to whether it feels “good” or not. It’s more like… I do it or I don’t.
Looking back, would you say that activities or hobbies you used to enjoy don’t feel as rewarding or enjoyable as they once did?
I don’t know… maybe. I can’t really tell. I don’t think about it that way much.
When you do things now, like watching something or just spending time, do they feel less enjoyable or rewarding compared to how they felt before this low mood started?
I’m not really sure. I guess I haven’t noticed a clear difference… it mostly just feels like passing time.
When you do things now, like watching something or just spending time, do they feel less enjoyable or rewarding compared to how they felt before this low mood started?
I don’t really know. It’s hard for me to compare it to before. I mostly just do stuff to get through the time, I guess.
When you do things now, like watching something or spending time, do they feel less enjoyable or rewarding compared to how they felt before this low mood started?
I’m not sure. I know I’ve already kind of said that, but… I just don’t really notice it like that. It’s more like I do things and they’re just there.
When you watch something or do anything now, do you find that you don’t really care about it or feel anything from it while you’re doing it?
I don’t know… maybe. I’m not really paying that much attention to it, I guess. I’ll watch something and it’s just kind of on.
When something good happens, like spending time with someone you care about or finishing a task, do you find that you still don’t feel much, even for a short time?
I’m not really sure. I don’t think I pay attention to it like that… if something good happens, it’s just kind of over and then I move on.

When something positive happens, like achieving something you wanted or spending time with someone you care about, do you find that you still don’t feel any real sense of joy or happiness, even for a short time?
I don’t know. I guess I don’t really think about whether it’s joy or not… it’s just something that happens, and then it passes.
When something really good happens, like receiving praise or spending time with someone you care about, do you find that you don’t feel much of anything, even for a little while?
I’m… not sure. I don’t really notice it in the moment. Like if someone says something nice, I just kind of take it and move on.
Looking back, would you say that activities or hobbies you used to enjoy don’t feel as rewarding or enjoyable as they once did?
I’m not sure. I mean… I don’t really think about hobbies that much anymore. I guess I just do things if I have to, or I don’t. Hard to say if it feels different.
When something really positive happens, like achieving a goal or spending time with someone you care about, do you find that you don’t feel any real change in your mood, even for a short time?
I don’t really know. I don’t pay that much attention to it, I guess. If something good happens, it’s just… okay, and then I move on.
Looking back, would you say that things you used to find pleasurable, like hobbies or time with friends, feel completely empty or without any joy for you now?
I don’t know if I’d say completely empty. I just… don’t really think about it that way. I haven’t noticed much, I guess.
Over the past two years, would you say that your mood has been consistently low without any significant periods of improvement, even for a few weeks?
Yeah… it’s been pretty steady, I guess. About two years now. Maybe a little over—like two years and a couple months, since the staffing changed at the clinic and my schedule got all over the place.
